_doc: M7-07 — the strings the Perk Draft screen (S07) shows, and nothing else. It exists because X-04 requires every user-facing string to be a loc key in EN and DE from day one, and because ContentInvariants.CheckLocaleKeyReferences fails a loc key that nothing in the content set names — a key referenced only from C# is an orphan, and an orphan is fatal. This document is that naming. The `label` group carries CAPTIONS only: the reroll's price and the skip's reward are tunables read from the draft economy and drawn beside these words, never written into them, because a magnitude inside a translated string cannot be tuned and would be wrong in two languages at once. The three DRAFT guarantee captions in `label` are what 24 §1.1 requires on this screen: its Visibility rule is a 🔒 — every counter shown to the player ALWAYS, as a plain sentence with a real number, because a hidden pity system is indistinguishable from no pity system — and its Disclosure rule makes stating every N in §4 on its class's own screen a store-policy requirement on both platforms. DRAFT is the class and S07 is the screen. They are captions like the reroll price's: the live countdown and the authored rung are drawn beside them from `DraftView.Guarantees`, never written into the string. Only three of §4.7's five rules get a row, because the Sustain anti-brick is a state predicate and the Codex bias is a weight and neither counts anything. ⚠️ Those three counters are not a free-reroll count: the counters exist and force real options, while the free-reroll allowance the design describes exists nowhere — the reroll charges Gold on every call, uncapped. `block.guaranteeNotDue` is the one absence with a sentence, because it is an absence in a mechanic that IS built: the upgrade famine is live and simply cannot be owed by a run holding no perk below its top tier, so its row shows its authored rung with no countdown and this sentence says why. Deliberately absent, each because it is unreachable rather than forgotten: a remaining-free-rerolls count (no counter exists in the rules layer, so there is no number to show), a per-draft reroll cap (there is none), anything ad-shaped — a control, a caption or a sentence — because the ad reward command is not built and a screen naming one advertises a feature the game does not have, and the perks' own names and effect sentences (those are the perk catalogue's, rendered with the tier's authored numbers substituted — and named as unavailable by the `effectNumbersUnavailable` line for the four shipped perks whose description tokens name no field in their own effect data).
